articles.author: Peter + AI
articles.description:
📝 This blog post was created with AI assistance to help explain technical concepts in simple terms.
Uniface is a 4GL (Fourth Generation Language) development platform used for building business applications. Think of it as a toolkit that helps developers create software without writing complex low-level code. It's particularly popular in enterprise environments where rapid application development is needed.
ProcScript is the programming language used within Uniface applications. It's like the "brain" that tells your application what to do. ProcScript contains many built-in functions (pre-written pieces of code) that make common programming tasks easier.
The $concat function is a string concatenation tool in Uniface 10.4. But what does "concatenation" mean? 🤔 Simply put, it means joining or combining multiple pieces of text together into one longer text.
$concat(String1, String2, String3, String4, String5)
  🔢 Combines up to 5 strings at once
  📝 Takes text inputs called parameters

  ↩️ Returns one combined string as output
  🌐 Works in all Uniface component types
vString1 = "Hello "
vString1 = "Uniface "
vUserName = "John"
The $concat function is perfect for:
  🏷️ Creating dynamic labels and messages
  📄 Building file paths and URLs
  📊 Formatting report headers
  💬 Constructing user notifications
  🔗 Combining database field values
  🚫 Limited to 5 strings maximum per function call
  📝 All parameters must be string data type

  🔄 For more than 5 strings, chain multiple $concat calls
  ✅ Available in all Uniface component types
The $concat function in Uniface 10.4 is a straightforward but powerful tool for combining text strings. Whether you're building user messages, creating file paths, or formatting data for display, this function provides a clean and efficient way to merge multiple text pieces into one cohesive string. 🚀
Remember: good code is readable code, and using descriptive variable names with $concat makes your ProcScript much easier to understand and maintain! 💪
articles.title: 🔗 Understanding Uniface $concat Function: String Concatenation Made Easy

articles.author: Gerald
articles.description:
Resolving Gmail Rejection on HestiaCP (Exim4)



  
  
  The Issue


When attempting to send emails from Gmail to a mail server hosted on EC2 with HestiaCP, the messages were being rejected with the following error:

550 Rejected because xxx.xx.xxx.xx(gmail's IP address) is in a black list at zen.spamhaus.org

This happened because Exim4 was configured to block incoming messages from IPs listed on Spamhaus, which occasionally includes Gmail’s sending IPs.
HestiaCP’s default Exim templates include a dnslists (RBL) check against Spamhaus (zen.spamhaus.org). Since Gmail’s IP addresses can sometimes appear in this list, legitimate emails were being denied.
Find the Exim configuration or template file
The RBL rule is likely located in the Exim configuration template:
 nano /etc/exim4/exim4.conf.template

To verify, search for the Spamhaus entry:
 grep -R "zen.spamhaus.org" /etc/exim4/

Modify the RBL block
You should find a section similar to this:
   deny message = rejected because $sender_host_address is in a black list at $dnslist_domain
       dnslists = zen.spamhaus.org

Option A – Disable completely
 # deny message = rejected because $sender_host_address is in a black list at $dnslist_domain
 #     dnslists = zen.spamhaus.org

Option B – Change to warnings
deny with warn so suspicious emails are flagged but not blocked:
 warn dnslists = zen.spamhaus.org
      add_header = X-RBL-Warning: $sender_host_address is listed at $dnslist_domain

Rebuild and restart Exim
Apply the changes with:
   update-exim4.conf
   systemctl restart exim4

Gmail messages can now be delivered successfully to your EC2 mail server.
Exim no longer blocks Gmail IPs just because they appear in Spamhaus.
If you use the warn approach, questionable emails are tagged rather than rejected.
These changes only affect inbound mail filtering.
Outbound delivery still requires correct DNS configuration (PTR, SPF, DKIM, DMARC) and may also need AWS SMTP unblocking or an SES relay.
Notes: Leaving this here for future reference. Ps ✌️
articles.title: Resolving Gmail Rejection on HestiaCP - Exim4

$acos(X)
